I submitted this mostly because I wanted to share my own experience. Warning: The Walking Dead (TV show) spoilers ahead.

I only recently started watching The Walking Dead, about a few months ago, after the 5th season had already aired. I really liked Lori's character to begin with, because she made amends with Rick, and she was the closest the group had to a peacemaker. Her death was the first one to make me cry. Anyway, a bit before that, Beth Greene was introduced to the show. To be honest, I hated her at first. I thought she was a weak person. I was conflicted between Andrea and Lori when Beth was suicidal. I was appreciative of Lori for noticing something as subtle as the missing knife, and caring enough to help a girl she barely knew; however, I agreed with Andrea that someone's life is their own to take. Instead of understanding Lori and Andrea equally, I was angry at both of them. I was angry because I've been in that position, and I have (and still) struggle with suicidal thoughts. I didn't see it at the time, but now I realize Andrea was right. If she wanted to die, she would have cut deeper, like I could have taken more pills. hated Beth because I saw so many characteristics of myself in her -- I'm 16, a girl, from a similar minded family, and was bedridden due to anxiety/depression to the point that I wouldn't even eat somedays. I don't know when it started, but I grew to like her. From hating goodbyes, to not crying, singing and playing guitar, writing in a journal...well, I did/do/love/what have you all of those things. Beth is the closest I've ever come to liking myself, because we are (were) so similar. While I love the concept of the show, she wasn't meant for that world (and neither am I), but she grew strong enough to survive in it. She became a stronger person than I currently am, and I hope that when I am better, I'll be like the improved version of her/myself. I've often feared what kind of person I'll be once the depression is gone, considering my therapist and I have set a goal for myself to become more outspoken, since for years I've been shushed and told by my family that I deserved all the emotional and physical pain I received. Beth is the kind of outspoken I want to be. I admired when she stood up to Daryl (who, during that episode, reminded me of my alcoholic father). Her death hurt. It hurt enough to not see her for a few episodes, not knowing if she was alive or dead. At the hospital, after he boy she was with escaped, she smiled at him, as if it was okay to move on. It didn't matter what happened to her, she just cared about what happened to him. I can be too empathetic, to the point where I'm very naive. Beth started to trust Dawn, which made me hopeful for Dawn herself, and I don't trust very easily due to familial issues. Beth was so brave, I can't even write about her death coherently. I was so distraught by the last scene that I cried for hours, and even days after that. It's been a month, and I brought up this question because I started crying about her again today. I don't feel like I'm meant for the world the way it is now, but I have some hope that I'll grow into it one day. I think Beth indirectly saved my life.

Sorry for rambling. I haven't been able to watch the show since that last episode, but I'm far too invested to not continue it in the future. I don't have any friends who watch the show (nor friends who are depressed), and I don't often get a chance to write about things that I'm really invested in, for others to see. If you read this all, I'm really grateful. :)

I consistently see people striving for a work/life balance. What are the pros/cons if you do achieve such a balance? What are the pros/cons if you don't?
Is work/life balance a real thing?

I don't know if this counts at all, but my husband just recently quit his second job so he can be home more with me and our son. Money is a bit tighter now, but it's 100% worth it since we get to spend more time with him and he's a lot happier!

Everyone has his own balance, whether he chooses or not, that he can manipulate to the degree that he chooses.

Too much work or play can cause you to burn out, for different reasons. Spend 12 hours a day in a cubicle doing paperwork and you see how someone might become depressed. Likewise, too much of a good thing can reduce the amount of pleasure you derive from it. A good balance can enhance your life in all aspects--it is simply your decision.

I think a lot of it depends on your job, really. If your job has a lot of overtime, you're salaried, you work on commission, or you're self employed, you're going to have a lot more intrusion from work in your personal life. Add in everything that can be sent to your phone, and now your job can potentially have its claws in you 24/7.

If you neglect work, your career will suffer. You probably won't advance, may be slated for the next round of layoffs, won't get a raise, your business might fail, things like that. If you neglect your personal life, however, your relationships fail and fall apart, you'll be more stressed because you don't get enough down time, if you have a family, they will suffer for your choice.
You could maybe get a job where it seems no different than your life. As in, there being no jarring transition to "I HATE THIS PLACE!"

My work/ life balance right now is fucked.

I miss my friends and my free time. About a year ago I took a position in a quiet office where I sit behind a desk for 9 hours a day for a salary that was greater than what I was making at the grocery store. It feels as if I'm slowly losing my mind there. On top of that my girlfriend has fallen quite ill so I am supporting us. Not just monetarily, I have to also take care of the dog, cook, clean, do the dishes, laundry, etc. you get the picture. At 26 life has gotten real, real fast. I get out once a weekend maybe 1 or 2 times a month. I used to get out that many times a single week.

Do I like my job? Not any more, it isn't what I truly want to be doing with my life. With that being said I want my life to be my job - I am a creative/ designer and I can't wait to turn that into my full time job. Once my GF is healthy we will fulfill our dreams by traveling, creating, and helping people in need. Until then I'm just a goat trying to stay afloat.

To attempt to actually address your question: I do think it's important to have a work life balance. What does that mean? I actually don't really know, it comes down to the individual. You got to have fun in this life, but more importantly, you have to do what is TRUE to YOU.

The key is to get a job that you don't absolutely hate that has defined hours (meaning you're unlikely to be called in when you weren't expecting), and following the rule when you're working you're working, when you're not you're not.
I refused two very lucrative jobs because I don't want to work more than ten hours a day and on the weekends too. If I never be rich because of that, that is fine, I rather enjoy my free time.

Feeling guilty I grabbed the bottle and semi-dragged him out the door (he hates this procedure), and into the front yard because cleaning solution and ear wax usually go flying everywhere during the struggle. I was concerned because his ears felt a bit hot, so I took a close look to make sure they weren't infected and, since he was being oddly passive, proceeded to dump a crapload of cleaner down his ear canal. After holding down his ear for a bit, I proceeded to lift the flap and offer some encouraging words. I should have known he was just waiting to strike: right as I open my mouth he gives his head a really hard shake, and I end up with a mouth full of warm, perfumed emulsion of dog ear wax.
